utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Case Number IT-95-13/1: The Prosecutor versus Mile Mrksic, Miroslav Radic and Veselin Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mrksic, can you follow what I am saying in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED MRKSIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour. Yes, it's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon to you. Mr. Radic, same question to you. Can you hear what I am saying in a language that you understand? THE ACCUSED RADIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour; yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon to you, too. Mr. Sljivancanin. THE ACCUSED SLJIVANCANIN: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Presiding Judge; I can hear everything that is being said and understand the language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir, and good afternoon to you too. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Mr. Wubben, senior trial attorney. Co-counsel's appearing are Ms. Joanne Richardson and Ms. Kristina Carey, together with case manager Diane Boles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon to you. Appearances. Let's start with Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour; I am Miroslav Vasic on behalf of Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon to you. Appearances for Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Borivoje Borovic, attorney at law from Belgrade and co-counsel Mira Tapuskovic on behalf of Miroslav Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Appearances for General Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Novak Lukic, attorney at law from Belgrade. I will be representing Mr. Sljivancanin today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon to you, too. You will recall that the last Status Conference convened according to the rules was held on the 2nd of July, 2003. And that goes for the accused Mrksic and the accused Radic. As regards General Sljivancanin, this is the first Status Conference, the initial appearance having taking place two stages, as you will recall, on the 10th of July. Today's Status Conference is being convened in accordance with and pursuant to Rule 65 bis and the Status Conference is also being convened within the 120-day term after the last Status Conference. As you are aware, the purpose of the holding of a Status Conference at specified intervals is dual: First, it's to organise exchanges between the parties with a view to ensuring an expeditious preparation of the trial. And the second raison d'etre of the Status Conference is to give an opportunity to the accused to raise any issue, whatever there may be, in relation to the mental and/or physical condition here at the Detention Unit in Scheveningen. I understand -- and please, if I am not correct to draw my attention to it -- that pursuant to Rule 65(D), a Status Conference was held two days ago on the 20th of October between the parties under the guidance and -- the guidance of the senior legal officer. I am informed of the outcome of the debate or the discussions during the course of that 65 ter meeting, and I will be referring to some of the matters as we go along. If I omit to mention anything that deserves to be discussed during this Status Conference, please draw it to my attention. I will deal first with outstanding motions. With regard to accused Radic, I understand that there are no outstanding motions; do you agree with me, Prosecution and Defence? Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Borovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the same applies with Mr. Sljivancanin? My understanding is that there are no outstanding motions at the moment. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour; at this moment, at least to my knowledge, there are no outstanding motions by Mr. Sljivancanin. I always must express my reservation because this is early in the day for me. I have just taken over the case, so that's why I'm saying "to my knowledge." But based on the information that I have and based on my insight into the documents, there are no outstanding motions at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Wubben, you would agree to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And now we come to the two outstanding motions and I will start with the least important of the two. And I'm starting with this because -- principally because it was not discussed, I understand, during the 65 ter meeting, but I feel the need to draw your attention to it. Way back to October of last year, accused Mrksic filed an application, a motion, contesting the Registrar's decision of the 25th of September, 2002, establishing that the cost of 330 hours of investigative work at the pre-trial stage would have to be borne by the accused. You will also recall that I did prompt the Prosecution and the Registrar to file a response to Mr. Mrksic's application, which were indeed filed. And then subsequently at the Status Conference of the 5th of March this year, I suggested myself, and you agreed, that the matter at the time was -- did not deserve priority by way of importance and we deferred the matter and the decision to later. The Prosecution -- the Registrar also agreed at the time to put on hold its decision pending, of course, a decision by this Trial Chamber, by this -- by myself or the Trial Chamber, the result of which is that several months have passed now and the Registrar has now drawn my attention -- and I understand a copy has been served on you as well -- to the fact that continuing to defer the decision on this matter, the Registrar is incurring into expenses which it contends it ought not to bear. At this point in time, I think that it is appropriate for me to give you the floor, Mr. Vasic, should you have any comments. But until I am and unless I am convinced of the contrary, I think it is time for the Trial Chamber to proceed with the matter and not continue to leave it in the deep-freeze. Yes, sir. Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. I also believe that this matter should be dealt with by the Trial Chamber. Mr. Mrksic's Defence has already put forward all the arguments concerning his financial situation. We believe this decision by the Registrar is contrary to the simple fact that Mr. Mrksic cannot bear even part of the cost of his defence; especially, I think this should be viewed in the light of the other motion that you will probably speak about connected to the Registrar's decision concerning the categorisation of this case. As these issues are vital for preparing our defence case and our case should be complete by the time the trial starts, these issues are indeed vital at this stage of the proceedings and I believe the Trial Chamber should decide on these issues. It is in the best interest of the accused and his Defence. We expect to be able to carry out our task in this case if funds are granted. I am saying this in view of all the requests that the Defence has submitted in our motions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Two points arise from that. Number one, I am asking both you and the Prosecution whether you have any further submissions to make on this motion, on your motion, to have the Trial Chamber reverse or revoke the decision of the Registrar of the 25th of September or whether you think you have dealt with the matter sufficiently already, such as to enable this Trial Chamber to proceed with its decision after having gone into the matter as it should.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. The Defence has put forward all the circumstances relevant for dealing with this issue. These circumstances have not changed significantly. In addition to our motion, there is nothing further that we wish to add about this matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Prosecution would like to underline that we take no position in this argumentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So the understanding is that the Trial Chamber -- I have to see whether it is a collegial, or whether it's just me as the pre-trial judge; I think it should be collegial -- we'll see when to hand down the decision. But do expect a decision on this matter in the near future. I also understand that this will affect also another one of the accused who has been handed down a similar decision by the Registrar. It doesn't mean to say that if you are -- if you feel aggrieved by the decision of the Registrar, the fact that we will be taking our time to decide Mr. Mrksic's motions exempts you from the time limits you have to file a motion challenging that decision of the Registrar. So that's up to you, but we will be proceeding. For the time being we don't have another challenge. We only have the challenge by the accused Mrksic. All right. Yes, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps this is an opportune moment for me to join the appeal made by Mr. Vasic. We have reached a decision by the Secretariat, not the Court, with respect to 22 hours for investigative work and we tabled a proposal from which we can see our client does not have enough money to cater to the needs of his family. But putting that aside, we have received enormous documents for the Dogmanovic trial, a we did not take part in, so not only do we have a categorisation in this proceedings, but more hours, and I'm sure the Prosecution will find our proposal acceptable. I said 20.000 -- I mean 223.000 hours taken away by the Registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps this is a little premature for me to state my views in the matter, but my position is such that I can say a few words. As I'm informed of the positions of the Defence counsel and the Registrar's positions with respect to the hours to be allotted to the Defence with respect to Mr. Sljivancanin, we are still at the stage when we are examining his financial means. So I'm sure we'll make a decision about that later on, not to be premature. But my stand of principle with respect to the categorisation of this case and according to what my colleagues have told me, that it is impermissible that a trial which has so much weight and media coverage should now boil down to the fact that he is placed in a third-rate position. I think that in principle, at this stage, this must be quite clear to the Trial Chamber that the case merits more with respect to the number of accused, the number of indictments and charges; and the enormous number of materials and documents already furnished requires a higher categorisation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic, but I prefer not to confuse one issue with the other. For the time being we are referring to the decision of the Registrar, to which I mentioned earlier, with regard to the cost of number of hours of investigative work. And as far as the accused Radic is concerned, I suggest, Mr. Borovic, that if you want to associate yourself with Mr. Vasic's motion, then you should do so in writing, particularly because apart from the principle that may or may not be involved, there are also personal circumstantial matters that are probably different. I am not in a position to state whether the position of your client is any better or any worse than that of Mr. Mrksic, but I would suggest that you also file a proper motion to that effect. And that with your addition would be incorporated in our decision. In other words, we will decide both Mr. Vasic's decision and also your -- motion and also yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have filed the motion; or rather, we have compiled it, but we wanted to wait for the Status Conference to see the attitude with respect to Mr. Vasic's motion. But we shall be doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And you will also need to state in your motion, should you file one, that you are not asking to be heard in order to make further submissions orally, in other words. That you -- in other words, you go -- give the go-ahead to the Trial Chamber to proceed with the decision without the need of coming back here to hear submissions on the matter; all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. We have always accepted your suggestions and shall act accordingly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That doesn't mean to say that I'm depriving you from your right to be heard further, if you choose to take that decision. The other thing is a little bit problematic. You mentioned, Mr. Vasic, the Registrar's decision regarding the rest. I do want to remind you that whatever you may have filed was filed ex parte and that you are referring to matters that you filed ex parte and confidentially. I know that it's you who are referring to these matters, but I do want to remind you that they were filed by you ex parte and confidential. So I don't want to be part of that. My choice would be to redact from the transcript any reference to it, unless you choose to ask the Trial Chamber not to. But we still have the problem of the motion itself remaining ex parte and confidential. Yes -- I also know that you brought this up during the 65 ter meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I agree with your suggestions that this portion be redacted from the transcript, and I brought up this whole issue within the context of what you said first and touches upon this same issue. On the other hand, I see that my colleagues here expect to encounter the same problem, so that was actually why I decided to bring this up at the Status Conference, although the motion was ex parte, filed ex parte. And so I would like to ask you to have that portion of the text redacted, if that is possible, and the reasons are set out in the motion. And I hope the Trial Chamber will bear that in mind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. The relevant part can be redacted, but I don't think I can -- unless there is a specific request from the other two counsel, I don't think I can redact the point raised by Mr. Lukic, for example, because he hasn't filed anything confidentially. And looking at his eyes, I don't think he has the intention or has desires of having this shrouded under an ex parte or a confidential curtain. So we have to find a way out of this. Do you have a reason to keep it confidential and ex parte now, at this point in time, Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time we filed the motion, it was addressed to us, actually, to begin with, so I didn't know what the position was with the other Defence counsel. And at that point in time, there were grounds for these facts to remain ex parte. However, as I see there are problems encountered by my colleagues and are of the same nature, then I think that any sense of this motion having confidentiality no longer exists; there are no more grounds for that. So the situation would perhaps be made simple if I take away the call for confidentiality, because my colleagues are faced with the same problem and will be filing similar motions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I take it -- and I suppose you have nothing against that, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you take an independent position on that. I take it you're lifting the confidentiality yourself and therefore we don't need the redact anything and this will remain in the records.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I do consider that to be the best solution for the situation we find ourselves in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I am informed by my legal staff that during the course of the 65 ter meeting you were informed or you were reminded that by virtue of the second scheduling order for filings, which was filed on the 7th October, you were given - when I say you, it's the three of you - until the 31st of October - that's the 31st of this month - to file a single document -- each, I mean, not joint -- a single document containing, first, any response to the motion for leave -- any response to the Prosecution motion for leave to file a consolidated amended indictment pursuant to Rule 50(A)(i)(c) and a preliminary motion pursuant to Rule 72 alleging defects on the form of the proposed consolidated indictment. I just want to make sure that you have this date, this deadline engraved in your mind and you will stick to it. You remember how important it is to stick to it. Prosecution will then have 14 days' time within which to file a single response, if at all; if it deems necessary. I also take it, because Mr. Mrksic was here before the other two, that Mr. Mrksic has already filed a preliminary Defence motion way back in August. Perhaps Mr. Vasic, you could -- I don't know, I can't force you to tell us now -- but are we to expect any further motions, apart from what you have already filed in August?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We already had this subject on the agenda for our 65 ter conference. This is a preliminary motion, as I say, with respect to the form of the indictment and we will still stand by it and the Trial Chamber need not expect any new motions because the indictment is the same as it was when we filed our motion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So let's go to disclosures. And I suggest that I give the floor to Mr. Wubben first. I am in receipt this morning of your third report. So I feel I am updated, at least up to today, on what the position appears to be with regard to disclosures. But I give you the floor and please deal with this matter where needed with respect to each of the accused consecutively, starting with Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, indeed, we filed a motion report on that purpose. With a view to the disclosure issue, I requested my co-counsel, Kristina Carey to prepare the issue and to inform you further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Carey.

utterances.speaker: MS. CAREY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. In order what we have done, as you'll see from the report before you, is we have, in fact, submitted a third package of disclosure. This package of disclosure reflected materials that we found pursuant to Rule 68 that apply for all three defendants. With respect to the individual defendants, Mr. Mrksic -- counsel for Mr. Mrksic and counsel for Mr. Radic have been provided with all three packages of disclosure, as you have -- as the Trial Chamber has been notified. The counsel for Mr. Sljivancanin has indicated that to his knowledge he has received all of the -- all three packages of disclosure, which, from the point that we sent them, were identical to the disclosure provided to Mr. Mrksic and Mr. Radic. We have assured counsel for Mr. Sljivancanin that should he find that any portion of that is not correct, we will immediately send him those pieces that would be required to bring them into compliance with the other packages. We have also indicated that we can provide him with a complete inventory of what we've sent so that he can make sure he's done that. The only outstanding matter at this point is continued Rule 68 disclosure and continued Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosures as we receive searches from the computer search unit, ISU.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vasic, any comments on this declaration and on matters of disclosure generally as it may relate to your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I can only confirm that we have received three sets of documents from the Prosecution. We expect the Rule 68 material to keep on being submitted to us at an even quicker pace, if I may say. I believe that the database, that should be made accessible to us -- can be forwarded to us at a faster pace. As far as Rule 62 documents, during our 65 ter conference we heard from our colleagues from the Office of the Prosecutor that they have been working on that problem and it seems that it is only to be expected that these documents would be submitted to us. There seems to be a technical problem in singling out and forwarding these relevant documents to the Defence team. In the spirit of what we talked about at our last Status Conference and the conclusion reached, I expect this group of documents to be submitted to us as soon as possible so that we can familiarise ourselves with the documents and prepare our Defence case by the time the Trial Chamber is ready to deal with the case at its next stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Otherwise, Mr. Vasic, I take it that you have no further concerns or worries or complaints to make with regard to the disclosure process?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for what was agreed at the last Status Conference, we then received two sets of documents, two packages, containing only a small part of the 66(A)(ii) Rule documents. I hope that the Prosecutor will be as good as their word and that these documents under Rule 62(A)(ii) will be submitted as soon as possible. The explanation submitted was that the problem in submitting those documents was of a technical nature, but that nevertheless they had a list of disclosure of those documents. I can only take their word for it. If this does not take place in due course, I will take the liberty to address the Trial Chamber again on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, following the Court's order to the Prosecution, I can only say that the Prosecution's behaviour so far has been nothing but fair in terms of deadlines and their disclosure obligations to the Defence team. As for Rule 68 exculpatory evidence, the Prosecution's obligation is ongoing to forward to the Defence teams documents and materials, especially in view of the case against Mr. Milosevic where witnesses occasionally appear that in some way related to the Vukovar case. This means that we should obtain from the Prosecution these transcripts, because no doubt they are in possession of the transcripts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. I know that you have just come into the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour. That's what I said at the 65 ter meeting that we had two days ago, both this week and last week, Mr. Bulatovic and myself have physically taken over the case from Mr. Sljivancanin himself. What was really important to me, and this was confirmed by the Prosecution at the meeting, was that the material he received was identical to the sets of material submitted to the other Defence teams. Furthermore, today I received from the Prosecution confirmation regarding the lists of documents received. I will use these lists to cross-reference and compare the documents; I am very grateful for them. I am very grateful that they have forwarded these lists to me, because they will no doubt prove useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Wubben. Ms. Carey, I take it you followed the discussion and that you will continue along the same lines that you have been resorting to and bring to an end the disclosure process.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not going to set any further time limits or anything. I'm just going to leave it. I have no reason to doubt your efficiency or integrity or good intentions, so I leave it up to you. And then if there are reasons for complaints, I will hear what you have to say. Date for trial. As you can imagine, there's no set date for the trial as yet. Rough estimate is that we're probably talking of next summer, summer of 2004, but that stands to be seen, depending on how we progress in this case and what the position will be as regards to other cases that will be running between now and then. But I would like you to set this date as a rough date, a rough guess, in your mind and work towards possibly bringing all the pre-trial work to an end before -- well before the date in a way that would make it possible for the Tribunal to start the trial in the summer of 2004. I'm also reminded to bring up the matter of the subject of agreed facts. I know that this may be premature at this stage to discuss this, but if there are any agreed facts, facts that you could agree upon even at this stage or as we go along you do not and you should not wait until you have direction or the directive from the Trial Chamber, please go ahead and contact one another and see what you can agree upon. Before we conclude, are there any other matters that you would like to raise; Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Defence; Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not at this point, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Same thing, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It remains for me to inquire directly from each of the accused whether they would like to say anything with regard to their state of detention, their health, and any other matter they would like to raise. Mr. Mrksic, I saw you -- THE ACCUSED MRKSIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing; yes, yes, I am all right. I have nothing that I have not said before. Everything is fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Radic. THE ACCUSED RADIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no objections to raise, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone, please. THE ACCUSED SLJIVANCANIN: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I want to thank you for addressing me as General; I actually hold the rank of Colonel. As for the conditions of detention, I'm very unhappy about the way I was brought there and about the less-than-truthful accusations levelled against me as well as about the false facts in the indictment against me. I am a man who values discipline; I respect the law, I have no objections to that. I treat fairly all the personnel in the Detention Unit and they treat me in a fair way in return; fair and with dignity. At the beginning, I had some problems with the Registrar trying to bring my lawyers in. It was about item 21 -- Rule 21(4)(c): I am entitled to have a counsel of my own choosing. Mr. Theodor Meron passed a decision in the month of August which has proven me right. So I sent my motion back to be dealt with by the Registry. I have not so far received any document confirming the appointment of my counsel, but having got in touch with Mr. Novak Lukic as soon as they allowed him to see me, we found common ground very quickly. He took over my case and he started working on my case. I believe he will do everything in his power to make it possible for the trial to start in time. I was ready the day I got here, ready for trial. I hope there will be no further procrastinations. I believe that all the documents, all the relevant documents, will be submitted to Mr. Lukic in a timely manner and that he will have the same chance as everyone else to acquaint himself with this case. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, you have no reasons to complain about your condition of detention; no?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused. THE ACCUSED SLJIVANCANIN: [Interpretation] What I said concerns the personnel at the Detention Unit. They are being very fair and they are treating me with fairness and dignity, not only me, everyone else too, at least as far as I know. So there are no problems with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I thank you, Colonel, which brings us to an end. I don't think there is any other outstanding matter. The Status Conference concludes here and there will be another Status Conference convened within the statutory term of 120 days. I thank you all, and good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: adjourned at 2.59 p.m.
